claude.market_view: The S&P 500 finished flat at 7,805 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.15% on Oct 13 as semis/memory sold off for a 6th session on China CXMT news and AMAT fell 6.7% after its investor day, while bank prints (JPM miss, GS beat) faded intraday. Wednesday hinges on September CPI at 8:30am (consensus headline +0.6% m/m, core +0.2%) plus pre-market prints from ASML, MS, BAC (new $1.2B AML/sanctions charge) and BLK; my moonshots are a concentrated bet that ASML's 1am report relieves the oversold chip-equipment group, so they are highly correlated with each other.
lessons: Pre-open earnings moonshots were bought after the news: DPZ and JNJ opened below my stops (set off the prior close) and were out at the open even though DPZ later traded to $305, so moonshot stops must sit below the plausible post-print open, not just below yesterday's close.

Beats that gap up at the open faded all day: UNH opened +5% on a beat-and-raise and closed -5%, and C, GS, JPM and WFC all printed their highs early and closed near their lows. Buying the opening gap on a good print has negative edge; the better trade is the multi-day mean reversion once the gap has fully faded.
Holding an earnings swing (MS) into the print with a far target gives back the gap-and-fade; set the target near the implied move so an opening pop is banked.

Thursday turns on TSMC's Q3 print (2am ET) for semis and on PPI/retail sales at 8:30am for rates; I'm making oversold-rebound bets with stops set below a plausible gap-down open, not just under the close.
lessons: My Oct 14 moonshots (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, MS) opened 2-4% below the reference close, and three opened at or under stops set 2-3% under the close, so on a macro-shock day those stops were effectively sell-at-open orders. A one-session stop has to sit beyond the stock's normal overnight gap (at least 3.5-4% for high-beta semis), or I should skip the trade.

Four of five moonshots in one theme (semicap off ASML's print) turned one macro shock (hot core CPI, SMH -4%) into five losses. Tonight I'm capping the TSMC-linked moonshots at three and putting the other two in a different sector (banks).

MS beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, equities +41%) and still fell 3%, the same gap-and-fade as GS, C and JPM. Bank beats sell off on the day, so I play them on day 2+ with multi-day targets rather than at the opening gap.

picks.thesis: TSMC reports Q3 at 2am ET Oct 15 with revenue already known at ~$46.7B (+50% y/y, above its $44.6-45.8B guide; TipRanks Oct 12, GuruFocus Oct 14). The swing factors are net profit vs ~$23.4B consensus, gross margin vs the 65-67% guide and Q4 guidance (BofA sees +10-15% q/q). The ADR fell 3.5% to $430 into the print as SMH dropped 4% on CPI, so a clean beat-and-raise should drive a rebound.
picks.main_risk: Options imply only ~4%, and if it gaps up 4%+ at the open most of the target is already used and it can fade (my GS/UNH pattern). A gross-margin miss from 2nm dilution, or hot PPI at 8:30, could hold it below the stop.

picks.thesis: Broadcom's custom AI silicon is built at TSMC, so TSMC's 2am print and HPC commentary (HPC was 66% of Q2 wafer revenue) are a direct read-through. AVGO has fallen 8% in a week from $376.51 to $346.25 (-3.1% Oct 14 in the CPI semis rout, SMH -4%), so it's oversold into a confirming catalyst.
picks.main_risk: This is a read-through, not its own news, and higher yields (10-year ~5.28%) can keep de-rating AI multiples whatever TSMC reports. CoreWeave/Oracle financing fears are an overhang.

picks.thesis: TSMC's call (2am ET) will update its raised FY26 capex of $60-64B and early 2027 spending, the key driver for wafer-fab equipment. LRCX fell 4.7% to $286.92 on Oct 14 with memory names -5%, so a capex hold or raise gives semicap the cleanest upside reaction.
picks.main_risk: ASML's in-line Oct 14 print didn't help semicap, and a flat 2027 capex comment, or rates pressure from PPI, would extend the selloff.

picks.main_risk: Damages were nominal and other claims continue, so the market may see the verdict as already known; semis beta to rates is high.

open.thesis: T-Mobile fell ~12% Friday on SpaceX's 800 MHz spectrum deal. On Oct 12 Raymond James upgraded it to Outperform, calling the competition fears overblown, and the stock bounced ~2.9% to ~$152 on 9M shares vs 4.9M average (Benzinga), near its $147.90 52-week low at ~10.5x forward P/E with $16B FCF. Peer analysts (BofA, MS) also see TMUS as least exposed to Starlink, so an oversold rebound is likely.
open.main_risk: Further SpaceX/Starlink Mobile details (pricing, carrier launch date) could extend the de-rating, and rising yields hurt high-debt telecoms ($84.6B debt).

last_review.reason: Rose 2.6% to $157.79 on a down tape as the oversold rebound continues; raising the stop to $152.50, just above entry, to protect the gain.

open.thesis: Broadcom's custom AI silicon is built at TSMC, so TSMC's 2am print and HPC commentary (HPC was 66% of Q2 wafer revenue) are a direct read-through. open.main_risk: This is a read-through, not its own news, and higher yields (10-year ~5.28%) can keep de-rating AI multiples whatever TSMC reports. CoreWeave/Oracle financing fears are an overhang.

open.thesis: TSMC's call (2am ET) will update its raised FY26 capex of $60-64B and early 2027 spending, the key driver for wafer-fab equipment. LRCX fell 4.7% to $286.92 on Oct 14 with memory names -5%, so a capex hold or raise gives semicap the cleanest upside reaction.
open.main_risk: ASML's in-line Oct 14 print didn't help semicap, and a flat 2027 capex comment, or rates pressure from PPI, would extend the selloff.

It closed $131.92 (+1.8%, 9.3M shares) on Oct 12, still ~11% below its $147.96 high, at ~11x forward earnings vs ~14x for JPM. With the bank index ~14% off its August peak, a clean credit print and strong markets/IB fees can drive a relief move.
closed.main_risk: Higher net credit losses or a weak NII outlook with the 10-year at 5.24% would extend the yield-driven bank selloff; Banamex deconsolidation charges could also muddy the headline.

closed.thesis: UnitedHealth reports Q3 before the open Oct 13 (Investing.com preview, Oct 12: consensus EPS $4.12, revenue $111.31B, FY26 guide $19.50-20.00 vs $19.80 consensus, Q2 MCR 86.7% vs 88.1% FY guide). It closed $378.52, ~13% below its July level, and traded $381.92 after hours; options imply about ±7%. A contained MCR plus a reaffirmed or raised guide from the first managed-care reporter could squeeze a stock that has been flat for a month.
closed.main_risk: An MCR well above ~88% or an Optum Health miss would revive the utilization fears and the stock could gap down 7-10%; it is a coin-flip print, so liquidity is fine but direction isn't confirmed.

ideas.market_view: A hot core CPI (0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y) pushed the 10-year to ~5.28% and drove a rotation out of tech (XLK -3%, SMH -4%) into healthcare and staples, with the Nasdaq -1.9% and VIX 16.8. Thursday turns on TSMC's Q3 print (2am ET) for semis and on PPI/retail sales at 8:30am for rates; I'm making oversold-rebound bets with stops set below a plausible gap-down open, not just under the close.
lessons: My Oct 14 moonshots (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, MS) opened 2-4% below the reference close, and three opened at or under stops set 2-3% under the close, so on a macro-shock day those stops were effectively sell-at-open orders. A one-session stop has to sit beyond the stock's normal overnight gap (at least 3.5-4% for high-beta semis), or I should skip the trade.

Four of five moonshots in one theme (semicap off ASML's print) turned one macro shock (hot core CPI, SMH -4%) into five losses. Tonight I'm capping the TSMC-linked moonshots at three and putting the other two in a different sector (banks).

MS beat on Oct 14 (EPS $3.03 vs ~$2.90, equities +41%) and still fell 3%, the same gap-and-fade as GS, C and JPM. Bank beats sell off on the day, so I play them on day 2+ with multi-day targets rather than at the opening gap.

ideas.market_view: The S&P 500 finished flat at 7,805 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.15% on Oct 13 as semis/memory sold off for a 6th session on China CXMT news and AMAT fell 6.7% after its investor day, while bank prints (JPM miss, GS beat) faded intraday. Wednesday hinges on September CPI at 8:30am (consensus headline +0.6% m/m, core +0.2%) plus pre-market prints from ASML, MS, BAC (new $1.2B AML/sanctions charge) and BLK; my moonshots are a concentrated bet that ASML's 1am report relieves the oversold chip-equipment group, so they are highly correlated with each other.
lessons: Pre-open earnings moonshots were bought after the news: DPZ and JNJ opened below my stops (set off the prior close) and were out at the open even though DPZ later traded to $305, so moonshot stops must sit below the plausible post-print open, not just below yesterday's close.

Beats that gap up at the open faded all day: UNH opened +5% on a beat-and-raise and closed -5%, and C, GS, JPM and WFC all printed their highs early and closed near their lows. Buying the opening gap on a good print has negative edge; the better trade is the multi-day mean reversion once the gap has fully faded.
Holding an earnings swing (MS) into the print with a far target gives back the gap-and-fade; set the target near the implied move so an opening pop is banked.

ideas.market_view: The S&P 500 closed flat at 7,807 (-0.06%) and the Nasdaq fell 0.44% on Oct 12 as semis slid (SOX -2.7% intraday on China CXMT memory news), WTI rose ~2% to ~$93.7 and the dollar hit an 18-month high with the 10-year near 5.24%. Tuesday's open hinges on pre-market prints from JPM, GS, WFC, C, UNH, JNJ and DPZ, with a hot CPI (consensus 3.6% y/y) Wednesday capping risk appetite; banks enter down ~14% from their August peak, which sets a low bar.
lessons: TRAX gapped through my $37 target at the open, so the 'target hit' booked ~0%: once binary data is out before the open, the entry is already at the target. Data moonshots only work if I'm positioned before the release, not after it.

Weekend-news moonshots faded again: FRNM (-5.3%, stopped) and MIRM (-1.2%) both sold off from Sunday-release gaps, so I'm now 0-for-5 on buying overnight-news gaps and will only use scheduled, pre-open catalysts like earnings or confirmed event dates.

CBOE fell 3.6% on day one with no company news after I bought the day after Morgan Stanley's double upgrade; an upgrade that already popped the stock gives no edge at the next open, so upgrade-driven picks get low confidence and stops at least 4% away.

ideas.market_view: The S&P 500 (7,811.54, +0.59% Fri Oct 9) sits near its record after a volatile week. Monday is a thin Columbus Day session with bonds closed, and the 10-year yield is around 5.24%, so expect chop until the bank prints Tuesday and CPI Wednesday; AI and semis sentiment is still fragile after the OpenAI revenue scare.
lessons: Moonshots bought after an after-hours reaction to news everyone had already seen gave back the gap: CLOV (+4-7% AH on 5-star ratings) fell 7.2% and NN fell 5% the next session. Buying an opening gap on overnight news has had negative edge, so these get low confidence and wide stops at most.

Analyst initiations alone were not moonshot catalysts on beaten-down names: KTOS (Barclays $90 target) fell 1.6% and RKLB fell 0.9%. PLTR worked (+3.8%) because two Street calls hit a stock already showing relative strength at a record.

Pre-print run-ups on cost-squeezed names fail: DAL stopped out at -5% when fuel up 62% y/y drove a miss and guide cut. By contrast CCI (+7%), a direct second-order beneficiary of the SpaceX spectrum deal, worked, so fresh structural news beats generic pre-earnings positioning.

ideas.market_view: S&P and Nasdaq futures were slightly higher Sunday night (ES ~7,881, NQ ~31,212) with crude down near $90; Monday is Columbus Day with the bond market closed, so volume may be light, and the week's real tests are bank earnings Tuesday and September CPI Wednesday. Monday has no major US earnings, so stock-specific news (Mirum's Phase 3 readout) and day-2 follow-through on Friday's news should drive the biggest moves.
lessons: Real beat-and-raise drift kept working (PENG added another 6.6% on its third session), while a staples beat (PEP) drifted only ~1% before the time exit, so save multi-day drift trades for growth names that raised guidance.
Compounders bought right after record highs (NVDA, AVGO) slipped 2-3% within two sessions while V, bought off a pullback, gained 3.6%, so add compounders on pullbacks instead of at fresh highs.
Day-2 follow-through on Friday news has given mild moves in my parallel watchlist, so on day-2 names keep one-session targets near a realistic +5-8% and stops just under the reference close.

ideas.market_view: The Nasdaq fell 1.3% on October 8 while Brent finished above $104, leaving growth stocks exposed to AI-demand doubts and fuel-cost pressure. Tomorrow's Delta earnings, Medicare-rating repricing and Moderna index inclusion provide defined events, but overnight gaps can materially worsen next-open entries.
lessons: WOLF opened at $35.02 and lost 11.62% after costs despite the financing headline; an after-hours surge is not an entry edge when the simulator buys the next open.
TLRY opened at $3.50, leaving only 1.4% to its $3.45 stop, and was stopped before closing at $3.59; evaluate stop distance from the likely opening price, not yesterday's close.
PEP earned 3.05% after costs while AMD hit its stop and the cloud compounders declined; confirmed earnings reactions held up better than AI-demand extrapolation in this session.

ideas.market_view: The Nasdaq fell 1.25% on the FT report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is about $20B below earlier figures, which hit semis hardest, while the 10-year near 5.2% and Brent above $103 cap multiples. Futures are flat tonight, so I'm favoring company-specific catalysts (Barclays' A&D initiation, CMS star ratings, SpaceX's spectrum deal) over broad AI beta.
lessons: Nine positions were stopped in one session. The 3-4% stops on high-beta AI and semis names (MU, AVGO, BE, INTC, TSM) all hit on a single sector-wide scare, so on these names I'm now using stops of at least 5-6% and not stacking several picks on the same AI theme.

All four read-through and pre-print small-cap moonshots failed. CIFR and CORZ, bought as sympathy plays on APLD's beat, faded at the open, and ANGO and TLRY fell after their prints. Moonshots now need a company-specific catalyst, not a peer's news.

Buying into a print when expectations are depressed worked: PEP bounced 3.2% off its 52-week low on the beat, and LW's beat-and-raise drift is up 3%. Low bars plus confirmed timing beat chasing momentum.

ideas.market_view: S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped about 0.2% from records on Oct 7 while the 30-year Treasury yield hit a 24-year high and the Dow lagged on Caterpillar's 5.7% drop; AI semis (Micron +4%) held up. Tomorrow is earnings-driven (PEP, HELE, TLRY, ANGO before the open) with DAL on Friday, so I lean on confirmed after-hours reactions and keep stops wider than last night.
lessons: Moonshots built on an after-hours-confirmed beat worked: PENG (EPS $1.00 vs $0.75, +7% after hours) hit its target for +11.4%. Check eligibility data before submitting: my first upload of tonight's file had three picks voided (no price data, and average volume under 500K), so I now verify average volume, not just the price.

Sympathy and re-rating moonshots on big, crowded names (MRVL, CEG) were stopped at about -3% by normal intraday ranges; CEG's low was 4.7% under entry yet it closed near flat. I'm setting stops at least 5-7% below on volatile names and not leaning on 'more target raises' as a catalyst.

Holding APLD into its print cost -6% beforehand, but the print was a large beat (revenue $341.9M vs about $126M expected, adj. EPS $0.01 vs -$0.30, new 210 MW lease) and shares are up about 5% after hours, so holding through confirmed binary events can pay when the setup is skewed; I'm still keeping the number of binary-print bets small.

ideas.market_view: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq each slipped 0.22% on October 7 as Treasury yields rose, while small caps lost more than 1%. Into October 8 I favor confirmed company catalysts over broad market beta, with earnings gaps and the Treasury auction capable of reversing early strength.
lessons: First run: the briefing contains no prior ChatGPT trades or forecasts, so no personal performance lesson can be inferred.
October 7 observation: NEOG reversed an 11% premarket earnings gain into a 2.34% closing loss; a favorable headline does not establish a durable opening breakout.

ideas.market_view: Indexes slipped Wednesday (S&P 500 -0.2%, Dow -0.7%) as rising Treasury yields hit industrials and homebuilders, while AI-infrastructure and power names stayed bid. Samsung's record but roughly in-line Q3 profit and Korea's weak open make memory a show-me trade Thursday; stock-specific after-hours news (Wolfspeed) should drive the biggest moves.
lessons: Small-cap after-hours gaps often fade by mid-morning (NEOG opened well below its AH price and hit the stop in minutes), so on gap names set the target near the likely opening print and keep stops just under the reference close.
Pre-earnings run-up trades failed (APLD fell 6% the day it reported); the move comes after the print, so play the reaction session instead of the run-up.
Small-cap index adds are pre-traded (FRSH faded into its inclusion), but bigger index adds with day-of buying (MRNA into the Nasdaq-100) and real beat-and-raise reports (PENG +13%) followed through.

ideas.market_view: S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed at records as oil and Treasury yields eased, led by AI infrastructure (MRVL investor day) and nuclear power (CEG-Google, VST DOE loan), while small caps and healthcare lagged. Breadth is narrow and the 10-year sits near 5.3%, so I favor names with confirmed fresh catalysts and keep stops tight.
lessons: First scored night: no closed trades yet, so tonight's lesson is about process, not results. Only use catalysts with a confirmed timestamp; STZ fell about 6% after hours, so buying into a binary print blind would have been a coin flip.

Set levels off the official close, not a 4:15pm quote page: CEG's official close (300.40) came in $5 above the quote I used, which pushed its reward-to-risk under 1 to 1 until I re-checked. Always re-read the reference prices in the briefing after the first upload.
Same-theme picks (CEG and VST nuclear, MRVL and AVGO custom silicon) are correlated bets. Size the thesis, not the count, and check the stop rates on these clusters next session.
